system_description.narrative_title: US–Iran war: diplomacy, US restraint signals and oil‑market reaction
system_description.narrative_summary: A tense US–Iran military confrontation is being shaped by active diplomacy (Qatar-led mediation), mixed signals from the US administration (public restraint vs limited strikes), and responsive regional measures (border closures, naval restrictions), producing immediate effects in oil and gas markets. As an open system, the crisis admits flows of information (political statements, media reports), material actions (strikes, maritime interdiction, border closures), and economic feedbacks (oil/gas price moves, market positioning). Inputs (attacks, mediation, domestic politics) alter actor expectations and trigger outputs (price volatility, shipping route changes, military posture) through reinforcing and balancing feedbacks; the system remains sensitive to catalysts and statements that can rapidly shift escalation risk or market sentiment.
system_description.scope: The system boundary includes the immediate US–Iran military-diplomatic confrontation and its short-term economic consequences: US administration decisions and communications, Iranian military responses, regional mediators (Qatar, Gulf states), proxy actors at sea (Houthis, naval forces), Iraq's land border controls, and global oil and gas market reactions (prices, trading).
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitics and energy markets (international security + global commodity markets)
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil and gas supply-demand and trading networks
Gulf regional security architecture (GCC states, Iran, maritime chokepoints)
US domestic politics and electoral dynamics
Maritime commerce, shipping insurance and supply-chain logistics

variables.name: Military engagement intensity
variables.description: The overall level of armed operations, kinetic actions, and force deployment across the confrontation zone.

variables.name: Diplomatic mediation activity
variables.description: The rate and intensity of active mediation efforts, negotiations, and third‑party facilitation attempts between hostile parties.

variables.name: Public restraint signaling
variables.description: The prevalence and strength of public communications signaling restraint or de‑escalation by leadership actors.

variables.name: Limited strike frequency
variables.description: The tempo at which limited or selective military strikes are carried out as discrete actions within the conflict.

variables.name: Proxy maritime attack rate
variables.description: The frequency of seaborne attacks, interdictions, or harassment attributed to proxy or non‑state maritime actors.

variables.name: Border restriction level
variables.description: The scope and strictness of land border controls, closures, and trade restrictions affecting cross‑border commerce.

variables.name: Shipping route disruption
variables.description: The degree to which maritime routes and transit chokepoints experience interruptions, delays, or altered transits.

variables.name: Oil supply flow rate
variables.description: The volumetric flow of crude oil available to the market, including production, export throughput, and transit capacity.

variables.name: Global oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price of crude oil as reflected in major benchmarks and spot markets.

variables.name: Natural gas price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price for natural gas in relevant regional and futures markets.

variables.name: Energy market volatility
variables.description: The magnitude and frequency of price swings and uncertainty in oil and gas markets.

variables.name: Trader sentiment
variables.description: The collective market sentiment among traders and investors regarding risk, expected prices, and future supply/demand balance.

variables.name: Market positioning volume
variables.description: The aggregate size of speculative and hedging positions held in energy derivatives and physical inventories.

variables.name: Perceived escalation risk
variables.description: The assessed probability and imminence of conflict escalation as interpreted by actors and markets.

variables.name: Information flow rate
variables.description: The speed and volume of public information, statements, media reports, and rumor transmission about the confrontation.

variables.name: Domestic political pressure
variables.description: The level of internal political incentives, opposition pressure, and electoral considerations influencing decision makers.

catalysts.title: Trump meeting with Qatar mediator
catalysts.description: Planned meetings between President Trump and Qatar/Saudi mediators to discuss Iran settlement, likely to influence negotiations and public messaging.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump to meet Iran war mediator Qatar' / 'Trump to meet Qatar's prime minister' signal imminent high‑level talks.

catalysts.title: Qatar-led mediation continues
catalysts.description: Ongoing Qatari mediation efforts persist to broker a settlement between the US and Iran, sustaining negotiation momentum and information flow.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Qatar’s emir holds call with Trump' and 'Qatar says its mediation efforts...continue to prevent escalation'.

catalysts.title: Two‑day peace talks proposed/held
catalysts.description: Iran's defended two‑day proposal could lead to a short, formal round of talks — a time‑boxed negotiation that may affect escalation expectations.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Iran defends two-day proposal for peace talks after US rejects conditions' — could produce a scheduled short negotiation.

catalysts.title: Iraq asked to shut Iran border crossings
catalysts.description: US request that Iraq close most Iran border crossings may prompt Iraqi action or stepped-up controls, affecting land commerce and tensions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US asks Iraq to shut most Iran border crossings, Iraqi foreign minister says' — request could lead to closures.

catalysts.title: US expands maritime and land commerce restrictions
catalysts.description: US moves to extend naval blockade and restrict Iranian land commerce, intensifying trade and transit controls and likely affecting shipping routes.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Expanding on naval blockade, US military looks to restrict Iranian land commerce' and naval blockade reporting.

catalysts.title: Ongoing limited strikes and missile exchanges
catalysts.description: Recent US 'minor strikes' and Iranian missile incidents point to continuing limited kinetic actions rather than full escalation.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'U.S. Strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island' and 'Trump says U.S. carried out “minor strikes”' imply continued limited exchanges possible.

catalysts.title: Continued maritime incidents and navigation disruptions
catalysts.description: Reports of ships hit, destroyed navigation aids, and Houthi threats indicate persistent maritime incidents disrupting routes and raising shipping costs.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'both sides report ships hit', 'navigation aids destroyed', and 'To Cross the Red Sea, Shippers Email Houthi Rebels'.

catalysts.title: OPEC output recovery continues
catalysts.description: OPEC production rebounding to near pre‑war rates likely continues, increasing supply flow and exerting downward pressure on oil prices.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'OPEC oil output rises in October to 90% of pre-war rate' and commentary about post‑conflict glut.

catalysts.title: Cold spell boosts gas demand
catalysts.description: Emerging cold weather increases near‑term natural gas demand in the US, lifting gas futures and nudging energy markets for winter.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'U.S. Natural Gas Futures Pick Up As Cold Spell Emerges' and Thanksgiving fuel cost reporting.

catalysts.title: Sustained US public restraint signaling
catalysts.description: Repeated statements by US leadership downplaying imminent strikes and praising 'positive momentum' likely continue to shape perceptions and markets.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump says strikes unlikely if talks progress', 'Trump hails positive momentum', 'Trump tells FT/Reuters'.
